newsitem.title: FRANCE: Earthlings to get first chance to call ET.
newsitem.headline: Earthlings to get first chance to call ET.

text.p: Earthlings will get a first chance to send messages to space aliens this year on a rocket bound for Saturn's biggest moon, the European Space Agency (ESA) said on Thursday.

ESA said it would collect electronic signatures and messages and pack them onto a computer disc aboard the Huygens probe due to blast off on October 6 for a seven-year voyage to Titan as a "token of human life" in deep space.

"Your signature or message in space!" ESA said in a statement. "ESA is planning to fly a CD-ROM aboard Huygens, on which all the signatures and messages contributed by Europeans will be borne away to Titan."
The Huygens probe would be released over the barren Titan, the largest moon of the ringed planet, to "examine its environment and surface," ESA said. The CD-ROM disc would be a passenger aboard.

Huygens is to be launched atop a Titan rocket by NASA from Cape Canaveral in Florida along with NASA's Cassini probe. Cassini is due to orbit Saturn for about four years from 2004, sending back data and pictures.

ESA said the idea for the space messages was inspired by metal plates on the Pioneer 10 and 11 probes in the 1970s to carry a depiction of Earth's location in the Milky Way galaxy and illustrations of a nude man and woman out of the solar system.
The details of those messages were criticised at the time as unintelligible to many NASA scientists. ESA was not planning to send a CD-ROM disc player aboard Huygens to help any aliens decipher them.
"Today's digital storage technology enables a large number of signatures and messages to be recorded on a single CD-ROM for dispatch into space," ESA said.
It said the signatures and messages would be collected by ESA on a special site on the Internet computer network, "http://www.huygens.com". They would be accepted until March 1, 1997.
